display_name: Consumer Insurance (Disclosure and Representations) Act 2012 (UK) under one top-level goal — does the Act apply, is the misrepresentation qualifying and of which class, and what may the insurer do (Schedule 1 Part 1) — and those three goals

others: is a qualifying misrepresentation … given … and (cidra-misrepresentation.l4)
the insurer's remedy for … and … given … and (cidra-remedies.l4)

scope: Goal-focused, at the user's direction: ss 1, 2(2), 3(5), 4, 5, 12(4) and Schedule 1 Part 1 paras 1-9 of the revised text as at 12 August 2016. Inputs: the finding on reasonable care (s 3(1)-(4)), what the insurer would have done, premiums and claim amounts, commencement. Left out on purpose: warranties (s 6), group insurance (s 7, Sch 1 Part 3), life of another (s 8), agents (s 9, Sch 2), contracting out (s 10), variations (Sch 1 Part 2).

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this against the Act. An independent test pass was run on 2026-10-18 (tests-independent.l4, 106 assertions from expectations written before the encoding was read); none failed. Its remarks led to para 9(6) being added and the para 2(b) refund being capped. The conversion lost the Schedule paragraph numbers and the para 8 formula (F1). The pipeline has not been run.

forks.F1: Lost Schedule paragraph numbers and para 8 formula: printed order paras 1-9; X = premium charged ÷ higher premium × 100.
forks.F2: s 4(1)(b): a higher premium is a different term.
forks.F3: s 5(5): a fact shown decides; where nothing is shown, (a) reasonable-consumer knowledge and (b) clear and specific question presume knowledge.
forks.F4: Remedy is the most the insurer may do (para 6 'if the insurer so requires').
forks.F5: Para 2(b): premiums returned only to the extent unfair to retain, capped at premiums paid.
forks.F6: Para 9 rights only where para 6 or 7 would apply; termination barred for life insurance.
forks.F8: Para 9(6): consumer may terminate after the insurer's notice; 9(7)-(8) not computed.
forks.F10: Exported helpers do not check that the Act applies; the top-level goal does.
